summary.en: Pakistani security forces continue to repel Afghan Taliban infiltration attempts along the Kurram border, arresting militants, destroying Taliban posts and killing attackers after cross-border firing. In Rawalakot security forces killed 18 protesters, including four children, during demonstrations over basic rights. A bus-truck collision in eastern Pakistan killed 11 people and injured 33, while a shop roof collapse in Karachi killed one person. The conflict produced 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Pakistanske sikkerhetsstyrker fortsetter å avvise afghanske Taliban-forsøk på infiltrasjon langs Kurram-grensen, arrestere militante, ødelegge Taliban-poster og drepe angripere etter grense­skudd. I Rawalakot drepte sikkerhetsstyrker 18 demonstranter, inkludert fire barn, under protester over grunnleggende rettigheter. En kollisjon mellom buss og lastebil i Øst-Pakistan drepte 11 personer og såret 33, mens et tak på en butikk i Karachi kollapset og drepte én person. Konflikten førte til 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
